subject: Business management

objectives.name: Show that you understand business tools, theories and course concepts, and can explain the problems and choices businesses face; include extension topics only if you take HL.
Use business tools and concepts to analyse a problem or decision, choosing data that help you examine the issue; apply HL extensions only at HL.
Bring business ideas and evidence together, weigh stakeholder interests and judge decisions; at HL, also compare competing strategic directions and justify your recommendation.
Choose suitable tools and concepts to investigate a business problem, examine evidence from original and existing sources, and present organised work using precise business terminology.

notes: Maximum 1,800 words; only the first 1,800 are marked.
One real organisation, and exactly one of change, creativity, ethics or sustainability as the lens.
Three to five supporting documents must be attached.

25 marks across SEVEN criteria A-G, common to SL and HL under the 2024 guide. Both figures are corroborated: knowledge base 7.7 [OFFICIAL] and two independent sources give 25, and a published grader rubric plus a second source both reference a Criterion G. The earlier claim of four criteria totalling 20 marks is the outlier and is now ruled out.

The per-criterion SPLIT is still not publishable. The one source that lists all seven marks sums them to 27, not its own stated 25, and sources disagree on whether criterion A is the key concept or the context. Corroborated fragments only: key concept 5, supporting documents 4, presentation 2.
The official IB subject brief confirms the component (20 hours, 20% at HL) but carries no per-criterion marks, as subject briefs never do.
The public ibo.org subject page still describes the pre-2024 structure despite a 2026 'last updated' date — do not source from it.

Topic and objective coverage comes from matching first-assessment-2024 IB briefs in two independent school collections, not the public Business page that still describes the preceding structure. HL-only topic labels and objective scope are retained; research-time and assessment-time allocations are not syllabus topics.

The briefs publish AO1–AO4 but no per-objective percentage ranges, so objective weightings remain null. These objectives do not establish per-criterion marks; the deliberately empty criteria and their documented contradictions remain unchanged.
